Verified by static inspection (Read tool renders raw text; no literal non-ASCII glyph appears anywhere in the pattern) that the prior defect -- a literal glyph embedded between escape tokens -- is gone; the surrogate-pair range [\uD800-\uDBFF][\uDC00-\uDFFF] correctly matches any astral UTF-16 surrogate pair (e.g. U+1F600 encodes as D83D DE00, both endpoints within range) and \p{So} covers BMP symbol-class emoji (e.g. U+2600, U+27BF). Could not execute the guard directly: this agent's actual granted tools are Read, Edit, Write only -- no Bash -- despite the dispatch note asserting Bash access; verification here is regex-correctness analysis, not live execution.
